title: Where Will The Relief Come From?

Where Will The Relief Come From?

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 23 Nov 2026

Over the past couple of months, we have pondered how to best position for a world of falling bond yields (see What If US Treasuries Rebound?), a stalling artificial intelligence capex boom (see The Confluence Of Risks, Shudders In The Tech Complex…) and a possible rollover in energy prices (see As The Clouds Part). We came up with a number of options, including buying metals, metal miners, emerging market debt, Hong Kong real estate, Hong Kong-listed equities, and Indian equities… Aside from India, all of these recommendations have turned out to be total duds. Most disappointing of all has been the performance of the broader metals complex which, in the past couple of months, has gone into full meltdown mode: silver has lost a third of its value. Palladium, copper miners, platinum, gold miners have done almost as poorly. Gold itself (yellow line on the chart below) has performed as badly as tech stocks (royal blue line). Combine this price behavior with the sell-offs witnessed in the crypto world, the sharp pullbacks in the Nikkei and the Kospi, the faceplant in Brazil, and the sudden pressure on EM currencies and it is hard to avoid the conclusion that the markets look, and feel, unhealthy. So what is going on? And how does this unraveling stop?
